components.css: .ds-agents { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 3px; width: 8.5rem; } .ds-agent { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; padding: 1px 2px; font: 600 10.5px/1.5 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink-3, #8b919a); border: 1px solid var(--rule, #2a2e34); cursor: pointer; } .ds-agent::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #3b4149); } .ds-agent:hover { background: var(--panel-3, #22262b); color: var(--ink, #ece9e3); } .ds-agent:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--amber, #f2a33a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-agent.is-on { color: var(--ink, #ece9e3); border-color: var(--rule-strong, #3b4149); } .ds-agent.is-on::before { background: var(--mint, #43c08f); border-color: var(--mint, #43c08f); }

components.name: Jack States
components.description: Signature control: seven states of a 22px circle, with a cable from a folder jack.
components.css: .ds-jacks { display: flex; gap: 18px; padding: 16px; background: var(--panel-2, #1a1d21); } .ds-jack { position: relative; width: 22px; height: 22px; padding: 0; border-radius: 50%; border: 2px solid var(--jack-ring, #646b75); background: var(--panel, #131518); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-jack:hover { border-color: var(--ink-3, #8b919a); background: var(--panel-3, #22262b); transform: scale(1.08); } .ds-jack:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--amber, #f2a33a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-jack.on { background: var(--mint, #43c08f); border-color: var(--mint, #43c08f); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--panel-2, #1a1d21); } .ds-jack.inherited { background: var(--mint-dim, #2a6e57); border-color: var(--mint-ring, #358a6c); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--panel-2, #1a1d21); } .ds-jack.covered { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--mint-ring, #358a6c); background: transparent; } .ds-jack.pending { border-color: var(--amber, #f2a33a); background: var(--panel, #131518); box-shadow: none; } .ds-jack.pending::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 4px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--amber, #f2a33a); } .ds-jack.pending:not(.on)::after { background: transparent; border: 2px solid var(--amber, #f2a33a); inset: 5px; } .ds-jack.blocked { border-color: var(--red, #f06464); } .ds-jack.blocked::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 3px; right: 3px; top: 8px; height: 2px; background: var(--red, #f06464); transform: rotate(-45deg); }

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Patch Bay"**

The window is a rack-mounted patch bay. Library assets are rows, places (this project, the folders above it, your user) are columns, and a round jack at each crossing shows where an asset is live. The panel is anodized near-black in three stepped tones, labels are engraved in small tracked caps, and the only light in the room comes from lamps: mint for what is installed, amber for what you are about to change, red for what is blocked. A thin amber cable runs from a folder's jack to the project jack it feeds, so inheritance is drawn rather than explained.

The metaphor lives in the visuals and in the code, not in the words. The interface says "Assets", "click a circle", "Add a library" and "Review and apply"; it never asks a teammate to know what a jack, patch or bay is. Density is that of a working tool: 14px body, hairline-ruled rows, a matrix sized to its columns instead of stretched across the screen, and a legend that sits beside the matrix at all times.

The system is dark-only (`color-scheme: dark`), uses one sans for everything a person reads and monospace only for paths and commands, ships no images or icon fonts, and runs under a self-only content policy with no external fonts or scripts.
keyCharacteristics: Stepped panel tones and 1px hairlines carry all structure; one modal casts the only shadow.
Color is state: mint is installed, amber is pending or your action, red is blocked.
The jack (22px circle) is the signature control, with seven legible states and a legend beside it.
Engraved small caps label the panel; they never act as headings or kickers.
One authored motion: a new cable draws out of the folder jack in 200ms.

rules.name: The Two Lamps Rule
rules.body: Mint says "this is installed"; amber says "this will change, or you are touching it". Neither appears as decoration, and mint never fills a button.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Every color lives as a custom property on `:root`. A new surface extends that set; it does not introduce a raw hex.

rules.name: The Readable Ring Rule
rules.body: Every jack ring that identifies a state or a control holds at least 3:1 against the panel it sits on; fills may be dimmer, rings may not.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked caps label a part of the panel: a control, the matrix corner, a library group, an asset's kind. They are never placed above a heading to introduce it.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Monospace means a machine path or command. Prose, names and buttons stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every live count (asset totals, the routing summary, count chips) uses tabular numerals so it does not jitter as it changes.

rules.name: The Sized-to-Fit Rule
rules.body: The matrix is as wide as its columns and no wider. It is never stretched to fill the viewport.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels, bars and sheets are separated by tone and hairline, never by a drop shadow. Only a modal dialog casts one.

dos: **Do** show install state with the jack and its seven states, and keep the legend visible beside or above the matrix.
**Do** use the three panel tones and 1px hairlines for every separation; keep the matrix sized to its columns.
**Do** reserve Patch Amber for pending changes, the forward action, focus, the active tab and selection.
**Do** keep monospace for paths, commands and change lines only.
**Do** use tabular numerals for every count that updates live.
**Do** draw jack rings in Jack Ring, Mint Ring or a lamp color, never in a hairline tone.
**Do** use plain words in the interface ("circle", "install", "Review and apply"); keep the patch-bay vocabulary in visuals and class names.
**Do** turn the cable and sheet animations off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and keep state transitions at 160 to 220ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
donts: **Don't** fill a button, banner or decoration with mint; mint means installed.
**Don't** put a drop shadow on panels, bars or sheets; only a modal dialog casts one.
**Don't** place engraved small caps above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow.
**Don't** use a circle for anything that is not a state lamp or a toggleable jack.
**Don't** add raw hex values in component rules; extend the `:root` custom properties.
**Don't** lay out card grids or stack boxed panels inside the matrix or lists; rows inside a panel are divided by hairlines.
